page: Hetzner Cloud cax41 is an Arm64 cloud server configuration from the provider's Cost Optimized family, virtualized using the QEMU hypervisor. The instance is powered by a 16-core Ampere Altra processor based on the Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture operating at 2.0 GHz, configured with 16 physical cores and 16 shared vCPUs at one thread per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 31.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 1.95 GB of system memory per vCPU. The instance bundles 320 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for primary filesystem access. No dedicated GPU accelerators are attached, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

Benchmark evaluations show that the cax41 yields capable parallel execution across its 16 cores, achieving a Geekbench multi-core score of 8,500.0 and a stress-ng multi-core metric of 29,117.84. In software compilation tasks via Clang, it recorded an average score of 15,304.0, while key-value store throughput reached 22.71 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 16.72 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Uncached memory bandwidth measured 102.2 GB/sec for sequential reads and 57.91 GB/sec for writes.

Per-thread processing capacity presents a functional tradeoff on this platform. The 2.0 GHz shared Neoverse-N1 cores generated a modest Geekbench single-core score of 1,052.0 and lower performance in latency-sensitive tasks like text processing and small-model LLM generation (24.34 tokens/sec). PassMark memory benchmarking also placed in the lower quartile at 1,828.1.

Given its 1:2 memory-to-vCPU distribution and competitive resource density, the cax41 delivers high cost efficiency for horizontally distributed, multi-threaded workloads. The instance is well matched for software build pipelines, CI/CD runners, container orchestration nodes, backend web services, and caching layers that benefit from core parallelism over peak single-threaded execution.
